```{r, theme}
apatheme=theme_bw()+

        panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
        panel.border=element_blank(),
        axis.line=element_line(),
        text=element_text(family='Times'))
```

# Experiment 1
## Main effect of Agency

### LOAD IN DATA AND ORGANIZE VARIABLES
```{r, data1}
# Read CSV
morality1 <- read.csv("1morality.csv", header = TRUE)
```

## Demographics
```{r, demographics1}
mean(morality1$age)
sd(morality1$age)
table(morality1$gender)
```


## Create dictionary of codes
#### Agency (0: Low Agency, 1: High Agency)
#### Time (0: Immediate, 1: Time lag)
#### Decision (0: Deontological, 1: Utilitarian)
#### Redo (0: yes, 1: no)

```{r, categorical1}
### create categorical variable for conditions
# Agency
morality1$agency <- factor(morality1$agency, 
                           labels = c("Low Agency", "High Agency"))
is.factor(morality1$agency)
table(morality1$agency)
# Decision
morality1$decision <- factor(morality1$decision, 
                             labels = c("Deontological", "Utilitarian"))
is.factor(morality1$decision)
table(morality1$decision)
# Redo
morality1$redo1 <- factor(morality1$redo1, 
                          labels = c("Yes", "No"))
is.factor(morality1$redo1)
table(morality1$redo1)
```
#### See how well the five items hold together
```{r, alphafive1}
# Chronbach's alpha for all five questions
allfive <- as.matrix(cbind(morality1$feel, morality1$upset, 
              morality1$responsible, morality1$guilty, morality1$regret))
psych::alpha(allfive, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, 
             max=10,na.rm = TRUE, check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,
             use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
summary(allfive)
```
#### If we drop feel and keep upset:
```{r, alphafour1}
fourq <- as.matrix(cbind(morality1$upset, morality1$responsible, 
                         morality1$guilty, morality1$regret))
psych::alpha(fourq, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, 
             max=10,na.rm = TRUE,check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,
             use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
```
#### If we also drop upset:
```{r, alphathree1}
threecog <- as.matrix(cbind(morality1$responsible, morality1$guilty, 
                            morality1$regret))
psych::alpha(threecog, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, max=10,na.rm = TRUE,
             check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,
             use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
```
#### This gives us the highest alpha and conceptually groups the more cognitive questions about moral culpability together and the questions about affective responses together.

### Create an average of the three items retained

## Means, SDs, and ANOVAs for each item individually
### General Feelings (higher score means more positive)
```{r, feel1}
group_by(morality1, morality1$decision, morality1$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(feel, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(feel, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
feeldv.aov <- aov(feel ~ agency*decision, data = morality1)
Anova(feeldv.aov, type = "III")
FeelPlot <- ggplot(morality1, aes(x=decision, y=feel, fill=agency, group=agency)) 
FeelPlot + 
  stat_summary(position="dodge", geom = "bar") +
  stat_summary(position= position_dodge(width = .9), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3) + 
  labs(x = "Programming Type", y = "Negative Feelings", fill = "agency", 
  title = "General Feelings about Programming the Car") + 
  theme(legend.position = "top") + 
  ylim(0,7) +
  theme_minimal() + apatheme +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_economist()
```

### ANOVAs for five-item aggregate and four-item aggregate
```{r, fivefour}
morality1$aggfive <- (morality1$feel + morality1$upset + 
                      morality1$responsible + morality1$guilty + morality1$regret)/5
fivedv.aov <- aov(aggfive ~ agency*decision, data = morality1)
Anova(fivedv.aov, type = "III")

fouritem <- (morality1$upset + morality1$responsible + 
              morality1$guilty + morality1$regret)/4
fourdv.aov <- aov(fouritem ~ agency*decision, data = morality1)
Anova(fourdv.aov, type = "III")
```

#### We also did this in excel so there is a variable named "moral" that is the exact same as this variable named "threeitem" and therefore either are fine to use in analyses and will ahve the same results.
```{r}
# average of the three
threeitem <- (morality1$responsible + morality1$guilty + morality1$regret)/3
```

### Main analysis of moral culpability 
#### Means, SDs, ANOVA, partial eta squared (effect size), Post Hoc Scheffe test, plot 
```{r, moral1}
group_by(morality1, morality1$agency, morality1$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
moraldv.aov <- aov(threeitem ~ agency*decision, data = morality1)
Anova(moraldv.aov, type = "III")
etaSquared(moraldv.aov, type = 3, anova = TRUE) # Effect size
PostHocTest(aov(moral ~ agency*decision, data = morality1), 
            method = "scheffe", conf.level = .95)
MoralPlot <- ggplot(morality1, aes(x=decision, y=moral, fill=agency, group=agency)) 
MoralPlot + 
  stat_summary(position="dodge", geom = "bar") +
  stat_summary(position= position_dodge(width = .9), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3) + 
  labs(x = "Programming Type", y = "Moral Culpability", fill = "agency", 
  title = "Moral Culpability") + 
  theme(legend.position = "top") + 
  ylim(0,7) +
  theme_minimal() + apatheme +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_economist()
```

### Logit regresion to check the effect of agency and decision type on whether or not an individual would prefer to change their decision (highe agency) or make the decsion instead of their CEO (low agency)
```{r}
binaryreg <- glm(redo1~agency*decision, family=binomial, data=morality1)
summary(binaryreg)
```


# Experiment 2
## Immediate vs. Delay

#### Load data
```{r, data2}
## Load study 2 data
timemoral <- read.csv("2moralitytime.csv", header = TRUE)
```

### Demographics
```{r, demographics2}
mean(timemoral$age)
sd(timemoral$age)
table(timemoral$gen)
```

### Make categorical variables
```{r, categorical2}
# Agency
timemoral$agency <- factor(timemoral$agency, labels = c("Low Agency", "High Agency"))
is.factor(timemoral$agency)
table(timemoral$agency)
# Decision
timemoral$decision <- factor(timemoral$decision, labels = c("Deontological", "Utilitarian"))
is.factor(timemoral$decision)
table(timemoral$decision)
# temporal
timemoral$temporal <- factor(timemoral$temporal, labels = c("Immediate", "Five Years"))
is.factor(timemoral$temporal)
table(timemoral$temporal)
```

### Chronbach's alpha for three items
```{r, alphathree2}
timecog <- as.matrix(cbind(timemoral$responsible, timemoral$guilty, timemoral$regret))
psych::alpha(timecog, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, max=10,na.rm = TRUE,
             check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
```
### Marginal means and full factorial means
```{r, means2}
group_by(timemoral, timemoral$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(timemoral, timemoral$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(timemoral, timemoral$temporal) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(timemoral, timemoral$agency, timemoral$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(timemoral, timemoral$agency, timemoral$decision, timemoral$temporal) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### ANOVA for aggregate of the three morality items
```{r, moral2}
tmoraldv.aov <- aov(moral ~ agency*decision*temporal, data = timemoral)
Anova(tmoraldv.aov, type = "III")
# effect size
etaSquared(tmoraldv.aov, type = 3, anova = FALSE) # Effect size
# Post hoc scheffe
PostHocTest(aov(moral ~ agency*decision, data = timemoral), method = "hsd", conf.level = .95)
```

# Experiment 3
## Predictions of other people's feelings (within-subjects)

### Load data
```{r, data3}
predict <- read.csv("3moralitypredict2.csv", header = TRUE)
```
#### Data must be in long format and was cleaned and organized in excel although this could also be done using the dplyr package.

### Means and SDs
```{r, means3}
group_by(predict, agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### Paired t-test
```{r, ttest3}
pairt <- t.test(moral ~ agency, data = predict, paired = TRUE)
pairt
```

### Cohen's D effect size
```{r, effectsize3}
cohen.d(predict$moral, predict$agency, pooled=TRUE, paired=TRUE, na.rm=FALSE, 
        hedges.correction = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, noncentral = FALSE)
```

# Experiment 4
## Test vantage point explanation

### Load data
```{r, data4}
study4 <- read.csv("4moralitythirdperson.csv", header = TRUE)
```

### Demographics
```{r, demographics4}
mean(study4$age)
sd(study4$age)
table(study4$gen)
```

### Create Categorical Variables
```{r, categorical4}
# Agency
study4$agency <- factor(study4$agency, labels = c("Low Agency", "High Agency"))
is.factor(study4$agency)
table(study4$agency)
# Decision
study4$decision <- factor(study4$decision, labels = c("Deontological", "Utilitarian"))
is.factor(study4$decision)
table(study4$decision)
```

### Chronbach's alpha for three moral items
```{r, alpha4}
s4cog <- as.matrix(cbind(study4$responsible, study4$guilty, study4$regret))
psych::alpha(s4cog, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, max=10,na.rm = TRUE,
             check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
```

### Marginal means and full factorial means
```{r, means4}
group_by(study4, study4$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study4, study4$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study4, study4$agency, study4$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### ANOVA on moral culpability and partial eta squared
```{r, moral4}
s4moraldv.aov <- aov(moral ~ agency*decision, data = study4)
summary(s4moraldv.aov) ## compare results for type I and type III
Anova(s4moraldv.aov, type = "III")
# effect size
etaSquared(s4moraldv.aov, type = 3, anova = FALSE) # Effect size
```


## How responsible do you think Alex is?
```{r, meansyou}
group_by(study4, study4$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(youresponsible, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(youresponsible, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study4, study4$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(youresponsible, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(youresponsible, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study4, study4$agency, study4$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(youresponsible, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(youresponsible, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### ANOVA for participants' judgement of Alex's responsiblity
```{r, youjudge}
youjudge.aov <- aov(youresponsible ~ agency*decision, data = study4)
summary(youjudge.aov)
Anova(youjudge.aov, type = "III")
etaSquared((youjudge.aov), type = 3, anova = FALSE) # Effect size
```

### Reformat data from wide to long
```{r, reshape}
widestudy4 <- select(study4, ResponseID, agency, decision, responsible, youresponsible)
head(widestudy4)
longstudy4rs <- melt(widestudy4,
                  # ID variables - all the variables to keep but not split apart on
                  id.vars=c("ResponseID", "agency", "decision"),
                  # The source columns
                  measure.vars=c("responsible", "youresponsible"),
                  # Name of the destination column that will identify the original
                  # column that the measurement came from
                  variable.name="perspective",
                  value.name="evalresponsiblity"
)
head(longstudy4rs)
```
### Assign level names to Perspective
```{r, levelname}
levels(longstudy4rs$perspective)[levels(longstudy4rs$perspective)=="responsible"] <- "firstperson"
levels(longstudy4rs$perspective)[levels(longstudy4rs$perspective)=="youresponsible"] <- "thirdperson"
head(longstudy4rs)
```

### Mixed Effects Regression
```{r, withinreg}
Withresp<-lmer(evalresponsiblity ~ agency*perspective*decision + (1|ResponseID), 
               data = longstudy4rs)
summary(longstudy4rs)
```
### Mixed Effect Regression Excluding Decision
```{r, withinregND}
WithrespND<-lmer(evalresponsiblity ~ agency*perspective + (1|ResponseID), 
                 data = longstudy4rs)
summary(longstudy4rs)
```

### Post Hoc Within Regression
```{r, posthocwithin}
PostHocTest(aov(evalresponsiblity ~ perspective*decision, 
                data = longstudy4rs), method = "hsd", conf.level = .95)
```

### Plot for Effect of Perspective on Judgments of Responsiblity
```{r}
PerspPlot <- ggplot(longstudy4rs, aes(x=perspective, y=evalresponsiblity, 
                                      fill=agency, group=agency)) 
PerspPlot + 
  stat_summary(position="dodge", geom = "bar") +
  stat_summary(position= position_dodge(width = .9), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3) + 
  labs(x = "Perspective", y = "Evaluation of Responsiblity", fill = "agency", 
  title = "Effects of Perspective and Agency on Evaluations of Responsibility") + 
  theme(legend.position = "top") + 
  ylim(0,7) +
  theme_minimal() + apatheme +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_economist()
```
